description: A stacked X-ray diffraction (XRD) figure of four as-cast Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe steels, plotted with the x-axis "Diffraction angle 2θ (degree)" spanning 20° to 100° and the y-axis "Intensity (a.u.)" without numeric ticks. The four patterns are vertically offset and labelled at their left ends, bottom to top: 0Be (black), 0.5Be (red), 1.0Be (blue), 1.5Be (green). A top-left legend assigns symbols to phases: γ (red heart), δ (blue diamond), Be11Fe (orange inverted triangle), Be12Fe (purple upright triangle), Be2Fe (green star), BeC (black triangle). Reflections are annotated with rotated hkl text: austenite γ (111) near 43° and (200) near 65°, ferrite δ (200) at about 44.5°, and Be–Fe compound lines such as Be11Fe (200)/(111) near 46–48°, Be12Fe (110)/(200), Be2Fe (211) near 72°, BeC and additional γ (220)/(311), δ (211)/(220) lines at higher angle. The 0Be pattern contains only γ reflections; 0.5Be adds Be11Fe and Be12Fe peaks; 1.0Be and 1.5Be show a strong, growing δ(200) line beside γ(111), and 1.5Be also carries Be2Fe and BeC markers. The figure demonstrates that increasing Be content converts the single-austenite as-cast structure into γ + δ with Be–Fe precipitates.

observations.observation: The figure is a single panel containing four vertically stacked XRD traces labelled, bottom to top, 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be, with 2θ running from 20° to 100° and an unquantified intensity axis.
The legend defines six markers: γ (red heart), δ (blue diamond), Be11Fe (orange inverted triangle), Be12Fe (purple upright triangle), Be2Fe (green star) and BeC (black triangle).
Reflections are labelled with hkl in rotated text, including γ (111) at about 43°, δ (200) at about 44.5°, and further γ and δ lines; no numeric 2θ value is printed beside any peak.
The 0Be trace contains only peaks carrying the red γ marker, i.e. the Be-free as-cast steel is single-phase austenite by XRD.
A blue-diamond δ ferrite reflection labelled (200) is absent in the 0Be and 0.5Be traces and appears, with the strongest intensity, in the 1.0Be and 1.5Be traces.
Orange Be11Fe and purple Be12Fe markers first appear on the 0.5Be trace and remain in the 1.0Be and 1.5Be traces, where additional green-star Be2Fe and black BeC markers are also present.
The caption states the figure shows X-ray diffraction patterns of as-cast Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe steels.

The citing text states that the phase composition of 0Be and 0.5Be steel is austenite (γ) plus partial precipitates, while 1.0Be and 1.5Be steel becomes austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) + partial precipitates.
The citing text asserts that the diffraction intensity of the ferrite phase (110) increased at 2θ = 44.67° with increasing Be content, indicating that Be addition promotes ferrite formation.
The citing text reports Be11Fe and Be12Fe compound peaks in the 0.5Be steel XRD, with an Fe:Be atomic concentration ratio of 18.7:1.
The citing text states that in 1.0Be and 1.5Be steel the Be2Fe and Be12Fe peaks appear around the Be11Fe peaks, indicating Be enrichment around Fe atoms.
The citing text reports that Be–Fe phase compounds in the as-cast microstructure are randomly distributed while ferrite is evenly distributed in the austenite matrix.

subfigures.description: Bottom black XRD trace of the Be-free steel; only austenite γ reflections (red-heart-marked) are visible, with no δ or Be-compound peaks labelled. Very flat background.
Second red XRD trace; γ peaks persist and orange Be11Fe / purple Be12Fe reflections appear near 2θ ≈ 46–48° and ≈ 85°. No δ marker is attached to any peak.
Third blue XRD trace; alongside γ peaks a blue δ (200) reflection appears at about 2θ ≈ 44.5°, and Be11Fe, Be12Fe (and a green-starred) reflections are labelled near 69–80°.
Top green XRD trace; the largest δ(200) line at about 2θ ≈ 44.5° and γ (111)/(200)/(220)/(311)/(222) reflections, plus green-star Be2Fe and black-triangle BeC markers and Be11Fe/Be12Fe lines.

unreadable_items: No numeric intensity scale is printed on the y-axis (arbitrary units only), so relative peak intensities cannot be quantified from the image
Exact 2θ positions of the Be–Fe compound (Be11Fe, Be12Fe, Be2Fe, BeC) peaks are given only as hkl labels without printed numeric values
Several closely spaced hkl labels between 2θ ≈ 43–48° and ≈ 63–73° are rendered as rotated text and are only partially legible at the supplied resolution
